newsitem.title: USA: Chinese man pays $450,000 settlement in CFTC case.
newsitem.headline: Chinese man pays $450,000 settlement in CFTC case.

text.p: A Chinese citizen linked to Standard Forex Inc, a firm accused of selling illegal off- exchange foreign currency futures contracts, agreed to pay $450,000 in a settlement with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the agency said on Thursday.
Yuan-Yi Lao, who lives in Beijing, did not admit or deny any of the allegations made in the CFTC's 1993 court case.

In its court case, filed with a federal court in New York, the CFTC said that Lao was a director of Standard Forex Inc, and operated as an unregistered futures commission merchant. Standard Forex allegedly sold illegal off-exchange contracts for the British pound, German mark, Swiss franc and Japanese yen until 1993, when the CFTC won a court order freezing the company's assets.

In addition to Lao, 13 other defendants were charged in the 1993 lawsuit. Seven have settled with the CFTC, five defaulted, and one man, James Feng, is continuing to contest the lawsuit, the agency said.
The settlement also prohibits Lao from making any public statement about the CFTC lawsuit.
As part of the settlement, Lao agreed to pay $450,000 to a court-appointed receiver, Samuel Abernethy. The money will be used to settle claims against Standard Forex brought by former customers.
